topics.title: National Affairs: Kishau Project, UCC, PM Vishwakarma and New Policy Updates
facts: India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on 12–13 September 2026. India holds the 2026 chairship under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”; initiatives include an infectious-disease early-warning system, logistics supply-chain framework, incubator network, Startup Innovation Fund, MSME Portal, smart-grid and energy-storage centre, Urban Mobility Hub and agro-ecology centres.

India and China held their first Corps Commander-level meeting in the Arunachal Pradesh sector at the Wacha and Damai border meeting points as part of military communication for peace and stability along the LAC.

Six states and Delhi signed an MoU on 15 September for the Kishau Multipurpose Project on the Tons River, a major Yamuna tributary. The project is estimated at about ₹15,000 crore, with a 232.6-metre dam, about 1,476 million units of hydropower and irrigation potential of about 97,076 hectares; the site connects Sirmaur in Himachal Pradesh with Dehradun in Uttarakhand.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated on 13 September that the BJP-NDA-ruled 21 states would implement a Uniform Civil Code before the 2029 Lok Sabha election. Article 44 directs the State to endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code for citizens.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting revised CBFC film-certification guidelines, including statutory warnings for drug or psychotropic-substance scenes and UA age markers of UA 7+, UA 13+ and UA 16+ under the Cinematograph Rules, 2024.

The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 is to take effect from 1 October 2026. Normal registration is expected within 21 days; delay beyond one year and up to two years requires DM, SDM or authorised Executive Magistrate approval, while delay beyond two years requires a Judicial Magistrate First Class order.

PM Vishwakarma completed three years on 17 September with about 30 lakh artisans registered. The scheme supports traditional artisans through skill training, modern tools, affordable credit, digital support and market access.

PM-Kisan Maandhan Yojana completed seven years in September 2026. About 24.96 lakh farmers were enrolled by February 2026; eligible small and marginal farmers aged 18–40 years with cultivable holdings up to two hectares make voluntary contributions for an assured pension after age 60.

The West Bengal Government approved a proposal for a DRDO weapon and missile-testing range at Junput in Purba Medinipur. It is intended to add a third major missile-testing hub for ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, air-defence systems and BMD systems.

A three-day Colombo Security Conclave Table-Top Exercise was held in Visakhapatnam on maritime terrorism, narcotics and human trafficking, IUU fishing and maritime security. Members include India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh and Seychelles.
topics.detail: The week combined BRICS diplomacy, the Kishau inter-state river project, constitutional policy debate, certification and civil-registration reforms, artisan and farmer schemes, defence infrastructure and maritime security.

topics.title: International Affairs: India–Vietnam, MERCOSUR, Space Cooperation and West Asia
facts: India and Vietnam agreed to observe 2027 as the Year of India–Vietnam Friendship, marking 55 years of diplomatic relations, with a bilateral trade target of US$25 billion by 2030 and cooperation in defence, trade, supply chains, connectivity, space, nuclear energy and culture.

India and MERCOSUR signed the First Additional Protocol to their Preferential Trade Agreement to recognise electronic Certificates of Origin and modernise customs and trade procedures. Authorised electronic signatures give e-CoO the legal validity of paper certificates.

The first International Space Summit 2026 was held in Paris on 9–10 September with representatives from about 90 countries. It focused on space cooperation, the space economy, science and exploration, space security and sustainability; 51 announcements were valued at about €20 billion, and India–France agreements covered launches, surveillance and microsatellites.

The Indian and Malaysian navies held the fourth edition of Exercise Samudra Laksamana at Lumut, Malaysia, with harbour and sea phases including cross-deck visits, subject-matter-expert exchanges, professional discussions and joint maritime training.

US President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 on 18 September. It expands sanctions and authorises tariffs on countries buying Russian oil or gas, making it relevant to India’s energy imports.

A UN fact-finding mission stated on 18 September that it found reasonable grounds for possible international humanitarian-law violations connected with US attacks on a school and sports centre in Iran; the Geneva Conventions of 1949 are central to civilian protection and treatment of prisoners in armed conflict.
India summoned Pakistan’s Charge d’Affaires after a collision between a Pakistani vessel and an Indian Navy vessel on 15 September, referring to the India–Pakistan agreement of 1991.
topics.detail: International developments covered India’s partnerships with Vietnam and MERCOSUR, space diplomacy, maritime cooperation, sanctions, humanitarian law and India–Pakistan maritime relations.
topics.exam: Focus on the 2027 friendship year, US$25 billion trade target, e-CoO, Paris Space Summit, Samudra Laksamana, sanctions legislation and the Geneva Conventions.

topics.title: Economy, Banking and Business: Fintech, UPI, Demat 2.0 and Trade
facts: The 7th Global Fintech Fest 2026 was held in Mumbai from 8–11 September under the theme “Potential to Impact: Agentic AI | Tokenisation | Quantum: Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance”. RBI recognised the Unified Fintech Forum as the second fintech-sector SRO, Bharat Connect expanded multicurrency forex services and SEBI launched the Demat 2.0 pilot.
NPCI launched Finance Model for India (FiMI) Banking, described as India’s first sovereign compact AI model for retail banking, and announced collaboration with HDFC Bank for banking use cases.

A new UPI Merchant Discount Rate framework provides no MDR for person-to-person transactions, a baseline MDR of 0.4% for merchant payments above ₹2,000, effect from 15 October 2026, and exemption for small P2PM merchants with receipts up to ₹1 lakh per month.
The RBI–SEBI Demat 2.0 pilot aims to tokenise corporate bonds and speed up settlement using distributed-ledger technology, blockchain, central-bank digital currency and smart contracts.
NHAI operationalised OneTag FASTag portability through the Rajmargyatra app, allowing users to change the issuer bank without replacing the FASTag sticker.
Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw flagged off India’s first salt-container train from Shivlakha in Kutch to Mithapur in Gujarat using stainless-steel containers.
The India–MERCOSUR e-CoO protocol will digitise preferential-trade and customs documentation.
TCS partnered with the Dubai Gold and Commodities Exchange to modernise derivatives-market infrastructure across trading, clearing, surveillance and digital or tokenised assets.
topics.detail: Fintech regulation, sovereign AI, UPI pricing, tokenised securities, FASTag portability, logistics and paperless trade shaped the week’s economy and business coverage.
topics.exam: Remember the GFF theme, FiMI, UPI MDR threshold and rate, Demat 2.0 technologies, OneTag, salt-train route and TCS–DGCX scope.

topics.title: Science and Technology: Semiconductors, Quantum Research and Lunar Science
facts: The 5th SEMICON India 2026 was held in New Delhi from 17–19 September under the theme “Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem”. Semicon 2.0 has a proposed outlay of about ₹1.27 lakh crore and six pillars: design, machines and materials, new fabs, advanced packaging, research and talent. The event had 600+ exhibitors, 300 international companies, 52 countries and 56 MoUs or strategic announcements.
CDIL Semiconductor in Mohali and Suchi Semicon in Surat began commercial production on 19 September, taking India’s operational semiconductor projects to five.

NIELIT–Infineon inaugurated a Centre of Excellence on Semiconductor Manufacturing in Ahmedabad focused on ATMP, OSAT, packaging and workforce development, with industry-grade equipment supplied by Infineon.

A Raman Research Institute team led by Urbasi Sinha demonstrated a single well-timed operation to protect quantum entanglement, offering an alternative to repeated error-correction interventions and addressing decoherence and entanglement sudden death; the research appeared in Physical Review A.

PRL Ahmedabad scientists identified the ancient Australe Basin on the Moon from Chandrayaan-1 mineralogical data; it may be older than other known lunar impact basins and is compared with the South Pole–Aitken Basin.
NASA identified a 2024 lunar impact crater called McGetchin from Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter imagery. Its diameter is about 222 metres and depth about 43 metres.
Anti-satellite capabilities remained relevant in UPSC discussions; the US, Russia, China and India have demonstrated satellite-destruction capabilities in space.
topics.detail: The science week centred on India’s semiconductor ecosystem, quantum error control, lunar geology, new impact-crater mapping and strategic space capabilities.

topics.title: Environment and Ecology: Himalayan Monal, Black Carbon and New Species
facts: The Himalayan Monal is Uttarakhand’s state bird. Researchers studied climate-change effects on its habitat and observed changes in calls associated with tourism and traffic noise; its IUCN status is Least Concern.

The A Resilient Himalaya report highlighted black carbon’s contribution to Himalayan glacier mass loss. South Asian black carbon was associated with about one-third of glacier mass-loss influence; brick kilns are major anthropogenic contributors, and black carbon is a short-lived climate pollutant with strong warming impact.

Researchers from the Wildlife Institute of India and Uluberia Botanical Institute Herbarium recorded Ophiopogon japonicus in India for the first time in West Kameng, Arunachal Pradesh, an Eastern Himalayan botanical discovery.
Two new frog species were reported from Mizoram: Ingerana aizawl from the Hratdawng Stream area of Aizawl and Duttaphrynus phawngpui from Phawngpui National Park. The research appeared in Zootaxa.

Dryland Congress 2026 was held in New Delhi under the theme “Transforming Dryland Agriculture with South–South Cooperation”. The Delhi Declaration on Drylands (3D) was adopted; ICAR and ICRISAT organised the event, marking 50 years of their partnership.
topics.detail: Environmental coverage linked species conservation, climate pollutants, Himalayan ecology, new biodiversity records and dryland agriculture cooperation.
topics.exam: Remember Himalayan Monal status and state, black-carbon sources, West Kameng, both frog species, Zootaxa, 3D Declaration and ICAR–ICRISAT.
topics.remember: Himalayan Monal: Uttarakhand state bird; Ophiopogon: West Kameng; frogs: Ingerana aizawl and Duttaphrynus phawngpui.

topics.title: Defence and Security: Yudh Abhyas, VIMARSH, AASHVAST and Cybersecurity
facts: The 22nd edition of India–USA exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026 covered Integrated Battle Groups, infantry operations, drones, autonomous systems, long-range precision fires and mountain or semi-mountain operations at Auli, Uttarakhand and Mahajan Field Firing Range, Bikaner.
India and Japan conducted bilateral air exercise Veer Guardian 2026 at Jodhpur. Indian aircraft included LCA Tejas, Su-30MKI and Rafale, while Japan participated with the F-2A.

DRDO–Industry Synergy Meet VIMARSH 2026 was held in New Delhi under “Varta se Vikas”. Measures included direct funding, incubation, DRDO testing facilities and software source-code sharing for MSMEs and defence startups; nine LAToTs went to 13 manufacturing partners, and DRDO and QCI signed an agreement for SAMAR 2.0.

The Indian Army developed AASHVAST, a specialised security capability to identify vulnerabilities in unmanned systems, including foreign components, cyber vulnerabilities, drone security and electronic systems.
DRDO’s SHIELD programme concerns high-power microwave technology, gallium-nitride-based SSPA and electronic-system vulnerability assessment.
The proposed Junput facility will expand DRDO testing capacity alongside existing facilities at Chandipur and Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island in Odisha.

facts: NITI Aayog and WRI India released the India Electric Mobility Index 2025 assessing 36 States and UTs across 16 indicators. topics.title: Art and Culture: Hindi Diwas, Hilsa and Sant Malukdas
facts: Hindi Diwas was observed on 14 September. The Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi as the official language of the Union on 14 September 1949; the constitutional provision is Article 343. Hindi was not declared the national language; the constitutional term is official language of the Union.

About 500 tonnes of Hilsa were exported to Bangladesh through West Bengal’s Petrapole land port. Hilsa is Tenualosa ilisha, an anadromous fish associated with the Bay of Bengal and Hooghly–Bhagirathi system, and is West Bengal’s state fish.
A commemorative postage stamp was issued for Sant Malukdas, highlighting devotion, knowledge, compassion and public welfare.

19 September: The main event of the Aichi–Nagoya Asian Games 2026 began in Japan, scheduled for 19 September–4 October.

topics.title: State Current Affairs: Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Other States
facts: Uttar Pradesh is a beneficiary state of the Kishau Multipurpose Project. The UP Cabinet approved an ethanol plant in Mathura, development proposals including Chitrakoot Link Expressway and an NSG regional centre at Milkipur, 20% reservation for former Agniveers in jail-warder recruitment, and concessional loans for small and marginal farmers under Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana.
West Bengal was linked to the Junput DRDO missile-testing proposal and exported Hilsa to Bangladesh through Petrapole.

Maharashtra proposed a ₹27,000-crore Greenfield Shipbuilding Industrial Cluster at Dighi, Raigad. Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders is to invest about ₹15,000 crore as anchor shipyard, with target capacity of about two million gross tonnes per year.
Gujarat hosted Suchi Semicon’s commercial production at Surat and the Shivlakha–Mithapur salt-container route, and was connected to the NIELIT–Infineon semiconductor ecosystem in Ahmedabad.
Punjab’s Mohali became a semiconductor-production location through CDIL; Kerala’s Cochin Shipyard and UAE-based Drydocks World signed a 50:50 JV for an International Ship Repair Facility.
Arunachal Pradesh featured Wacha–Damai India–China talks and the first Indian record of Ophiopogon japonicus in West Kameng; Mizoram featured the two new frog species.
Rajasthan featured Bikaner’s Yudh Abhyas, Jodhpur’s Veer Guardian and its beneficiary status in the Kishau Project.
